data.translation: Chorepiscopus Brahim: I stayed with my aunt's husband, me and his brother-in-law, I have told you, Yuhanun of the Təyyо family. We used to sleep there and study. He used to teach us everything he knew. Afterwards I searched through books on my own for nine years, night and day. I used to read; I am not telling you falsely. There was no electricity. The lamp, I used to fall asleep; the lamp would remain burning. I used to fall asleep over the book. That is, there is no falsehood!

rationale: New I.2 Infectum-wa box; first-person habitual sleep while studying, with both adjacent tokens retained in one quotation. No edition translation is available.

summary: I contrasts sleep onset (Preterit Intransitive), modal/prospective sleep (Infectum), ko-Preterit result and Part act. sleep state. Bare qaṭəl does not by itself guarantee a punctual reading.
Ḥəlle kṭawiʕo i ʕaskar uses feminine agreement with a collective; it is not automatically Part act. merely because a resulting state is described.
The forming of communion wafers remains II1; German backte does not establish a separate baking sense.
Read-only lookup of dmx confirms III b-ruḥe 'sich schlafend stellen' as an analogy, not proof of every unattested ṭwʕ form.

Existing references at 30/71, 48/71, 56/117, 61/149, 62/273, 67/34, 69/31, 519, 522 and 70/261–262 are not new examples. PrS 85/108 corresponds to existing prs 252/25. Existing notes and spelling irregularities are preserved.

Jan Beṯ-Şawoce provides no edition translation. English in the input is machine translation and is not quoted as an edition translation. Added examples therefore have an empty translation field; meanings are assessed from the Turoyo.
I Infectum sleep was already proposed in round 1; ṭəwʕi adds a thin-cell purpose context rather than a new box. I Infectum-wa is this round's new box.
The two ṭuwaʕnowo tokens share one studying scene and one selected quotation. Lamp burning contrasts with the speaker's recurring sleep; the lamp is not the sleeping subject.
ʕal u kṯowo gives location/posture, not a new object or idiom. No evidence here extends the round-1 III pretence construction.
Confirm contracted ṭuʕi at JTM 1.5/25 and ṭawəḥto beside tawəḥto/expected ṭawiʕto at 24/141.
Confirm maṭwaʕla as III in 96/307; only b-ruḥa pretence is attested. Its Infectum and an unrestricted causative meaning remain unknown.
Confirm kṭawəʕ (97/64) as ko-Preterit against possible Infectum vowel variation.
96/157 has an alignment warning: the supplied German adds fear/yesterday dialogue absent from this verse. Its translation is not quoted.
MAC Besim Martyrdom of Maferyono/19 presents sunset; the next narrative episode requests that the sun stop. Check whether this is approximate onset or a narrative inconsistency.
Confirm the reduced vowels of ṭəwʕi and first-person habitual ṭuwaʕnowo against other speakers or audio if available.
Sunset serves as a directional reference opposed to sunrise; treat nominal direction as an extension of the existing solar event, pending lexicographical choice.
